messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Problems postscript files
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Saving a spectrogram in a vectorial format (.ps, .eps or pdf) is not a
great idea. A spectrogram is usually made of thousand points. This
generates huge vectorial files, sometimes difficult to open with a viewer.

You should choose a bitmapped image format instead (.bmp, .jpeg, .png or
.tiff).

Actually, the best thing to do seems to use the .png format employs
lossless data compression.

Usually the following parameters produce a nice graph:

png("myspectro.png", width=1200, height=1200, point=24)
data(tico)
spectro(tico, f=22050)
dev.off()

Best

Jerome

messages.subject: problem with new seewave installation
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm brand new to seewave, and very excited about its possibilities. However, I am having a problem with my new installation (OS X, R 2.10.1, seewave_1.5.7, tuneR_0.3-0, rgl_0.91). I don't see the error message on the web or in the archives of this group, so I was hoping somebody could help!

I am not able to use the listen() function to play sounds which tuneR's play() can handle:

> library(tuneR)
> setWavPlayer("/usr/bin/afplay")
> library(seewave)
Loading Tcl/Tk interface ... done
> data(pellucens)
> pellucens

Wave Object
Number of Samples:      36476
Duration (seconds):     3.31
Samplingrate (Hertz):   11025
Channels (Mono/Stereo): Mono
Bit (8/16/24/32):       16

> play(pellucens)
> listen(pellucens)
Error in writeWave(object, filename) :
  for 16-bit Wave files, data range is supposed to be in [-32768, 32767], see ?normalize

I tried normalizing the sound, but to no avail:

> p2 <- normalize(pellucens, unit="16")
> listen(p2)
Error in writeWave(object, filename) :
  for 16-bit Wave files, data range is supposed to be in [-32768, 32767], see ?normalize

Does anybody have any idea what I'm doing wrong here?

Thanks very much!
Jesse Ross

Thanks for using seewave. This is a bug in the listen() function. This
should be fixed in the forthcoming release.
Try this instead:

library(tuneR)
library(seewave)
data(pellucens)

p2 <- normalize(pellucens, unit="16")

play(p2)

Jerome

messages.subject: Re: Temporal parameters
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tomi,

Sorry for the delay.
A solution for the buzzing part of your cicada song is to try to
analyse the amplitude modulation. You can do that with the function
ama().

Try this:

# reading the file
a <- readWave("DAT-Kreta01-36-B14.wav")
# selection of the buzzing part
buzz <- cutw(a, from=0.075, to=1.6)
# amplitude modulation analysis
res <- ama(buzz, f=48000, plot=FALSE)
# peak search
fpeaks(res)

On the resulting graph you see:
o a peak at ~ 840 Hz that corresponds to a slow amplitude modulation,
ie. the repetition rate of your group of pulses.
o a peak at ~ 1500 Hz that corresponds to a fast amplitude modulation,
ie. the repetition rate of your pulses.

HTH

Jerome
